title: Implementing a triage and queue protocol on a regional crisis text line: an interrupted time series and RE-AIM evaluation
abstract: Objective: to evaluate delivery, acceptance and service outcomes of a triage and queue protocol introduced on all shifts of a regional crisis text line in January 2027. Design: implementation study with an interrupted time series of weekly evening time to first human reply (52 weeks before, 26 after) and RE-AIM fidelity and acceptance measures. Results will be written after the vendor export.
introduction: Waits on crisis text lines occur at the moment of greatest need. Two recorded searches found no evaluation of queue protocols for text-based crisis services, so this evaluation relies on the line's own data.
methods: De-identified platform records without message text are analysed with segmented regression adjusted for demand and holidays; fidelity is computed from queue order and log-in times; volunteers rate acceptability at weeks 8 and 24. Analysis starts only after the data-sharing agreement is signed.
results: No data have been received yet. The report will present the time series, fidelity proportions, acceptability and counsellor overtime.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the change in waits against demand and season and explain any shortfall in delivery.
limitations: No concurrent comparison; English-only keyword flag; no measure of clinical outcomes after the conversation.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; limited to delivery and service outcomes on this line.
summary: StaRI-structured draft; the analysis waits on the data gate.
